column1: # labels.tsv -- THE ONE HOME of the estate's issue-label grammar.
# Zach, 2026-08-18 (hf7y/realisateur#397): "Repos need to look into a central
# place to see the grammar." NEVER copied into a repo -- read at the point of
# use by `etiquette`, the `discipline`/BUILD-DISCIPLINE.md shape. The verb
# build carries it, and a guard test proves the carried copy still matches.
# Columns:  name  color  source  meaning
# SOURCE decides who may write the label, and is the point of the file:
#   derived:decision  line 1 declares `DECISION:` AND nobody has answered.
#                     NEVER typed -- `etiquette --apply` writes it, reading
#                     bin/lib/body-grammar.sh and bin/lib/answered.sh.
#   written:<verb>    that verb applies it at filing time, and nothing else
#                     should. A human retyping one of these is drift.
#   typed             a person or agent applies it as a judgement. No
#                     mechanism derives it and none should claim to.
# A label NOT in this file is a repo's own business -- `etiquette` reports it
# and never deletes it. This grammar declares a floor, not a whitelist.
# NOT IN THIS FILE, deliberately: `blocked` and `question`. They were in
# scheduler's TEMPO_BLOCKED_LABELS until 2026-08-18 and meant something else
# in practice -- `question` was a TOPIC label (chezz #4/#5/#6). Adding either
# here means answering "who writes it, and does it mean a HUMAN is in the way".
needs-human
column4: Only a human can move this: line 1 declares `DECISION:` and no human has answered yet. An answered decision is an AGENT's work and loses the label. Subtracted from the actionable backlog by scheduler's tempo, so it is a real brake on dispatch.

column1: answered
column4: A human answered this, somewhere the predicate cannot see -- another issue, a conversation, a room. THE OVERRIDE for `needs-human`, and the only one: `bin/lib/answered.jq` reads comments on THIS issue and nothing else, so an answer given on a different issue reads as silence and the question gets asked again (hf7y/wtul#37 was settled on hf7y/wtul#34 and blocked nine days). Typed on purpose -- nothing derives it, and forging one is auditable while a lost answer leaves nothing.

column1: deferred
column4: Work parked deliberately, FOR AN AGENT, by `defere`. It is a queue, not a blocker -- it does NOT mean a human is in the way and must not be read as one.

column1: defaulted
column4: A `DECISION:` nobody answered inside its own declared `DEFAULT-AFTER` window, so the dispatch proceeded on the default and said so in a comment. REVERSIBLE and the issue stays OPEN: this is a record of an act, not a closure. It is applied only when the body declared a default -- a decision with none blocks forever, on purpose, because that is the correct outcome for an irreversible call.

column1: unroutable
column4: No repo owns this yet. Its own state, never a soft way of assigning to a person; the ownership gap is the finding.

column1: # THE DECAY-RATE PAIR (Zach, 2026-08-06, hf7y/vim-arcade#77): FIFO over the
# backlog is incoherent because it mixes two populations that rot at different
# rates. `decayable` and `durable` are that vocabulary -- deliberately two
# names, not a taxonomy, and at most one per issue. The reader is
# vim_arcade/issue_types.py (TYPE_LABELS), which is where the mutual exclusion
# is enforced; `etiquette --apply` only has to make the labels EXIST, because
# `gh issue edit --add-label` fails on a repo that lacks them and that failure
# is what left the dashboard's type key dead in 24 of 24 repos.
# WHAT THE PAIR IS FOR RIGHT NOW (2026-08-26): the v1 freeze. realisateur takes
# `durable` only; `decayable` goes to hf7y/scheduler, where v2 lives. Both stay
# `typed` -- nothing derives them and nothing new writes them, so the "who
# writes it" question above is answered unchanged. The freeze is enforced by
# the monthly cut (realisateur#602), not by these labels: they sort the queue,
# they do not gate it. BUILD-DISCIPLINE.md's protocols block carries the rule.
decayable
column4: An idea or build that may already be obviated by the time it is reached. Mutually exclusive with `durable`.

column1: durable
column4: A bug, broken guard, or missing credential: stays exactly as broken until fixed. Mutually exclusive with `decayable`.
